title: Nau Devi Yatra (9 Devi Yatra): Nine Devis, Route, Timings & Days
seo_title: Nau Devi Yatra (9 Devi Yatra): Temples, Route & Days
seo_desc: Nau Devi Yatra guide: the nine Devi temples from Shakumbhari to Vaishno Devi, route with road km, darshan timings, a 9-day itinerary and Navratri tips.
label: Nau Devi Yatra
blurb: Nine Devis, from Shakumbhari to Vaishno Devi
kicker: Nine Devis · Himachal, Haryana, UP & Jammu
sub: The nine Devi temples of North India's best-loved yatra — which nine, in what order, how many days, darshan hours from the shrine boards, the Vaishno Devi RFID card and how to plan around Navratri. Written by Suzu Travels, from Bilaspur.
q: What is the Nau Devi Yatra?
answer: The Nau Devi Yatra (9 Devi Yatra) is a road pilgrimage to nine Devi temples of the North Indian hills: Shakumbhari, Mansa Devi (Panchkula), Kali Mata of Kalka, Naina Devi, Chintpurni, Jwala Ji, Brajeshwari (Kangra), Chamunda and Vaishno Devi. All nine take about 9 days from Delhi; the shorter package route of seven Devis takes about 7 days from Chandigarh.
facts: in the classical Shakti Peeth lists
free RFID card for Vaishno Devi only
intro: Hindi pamphlets and family stories call the hill goddesses Saat Behna, the seven sisters, with Mata Vaishno Devi as the eldest. Over time the seven grew to nine — Kali Mata of Kalka and Shakumbhari Devi were added — so that a family could take one darshan for each night of Navratri. That is the yatra this guide follows, with the common package variant explained below.
Five of the nine are in Himachal and also make up our 5 Shakti Peeths of Himachal circuit. For the wider sacred map, see the pilgrimage hub.

story.h2: The nine Devis and their stories
story.lead: No single legend links all nine shrines. Each temple keeps its own story — here they are in our own words, as tradition tells them.
beats: When Shiva carried Sati's body across the worlds, Vishnu's chakra divided it. Tradition places her eyes at Naina Devi, her tongue at Jwala Ji and her left breast at Brajeshwari in Kangra.
In the hills the Devis are spoken of as seven sisters — Saat Behna — with Mata Vaishno Devi, in her cave on Trikuta hill, as the eldest.
The Devi Bhagavata tells of Shakumbhari, the hundred-eyed Mother, whose tears ended a hundred-year famine and who fed the world with vegetables and herbs.
Kali of Kalka, Chamunda and Chintpurni

Kali of Kalka is believed to have destroyed the demons who drove the gods into the hills; Chamunda slew Chanda and Munda; and at Chintpurni the Devi is said to have freed her devotee Mai Das of all worry.
more: Only Naina Devi, Jwala Ji and Brajeshwari appear in the compiled lists of the 51 Shakti Peeths, and Chintpurni's place is disputed. Vaishno Devi, Mansa Devi, Chamunda, Kalka and Shakumbhari are deeply revered shrines by their own traditions — we say so plainly rather than call all nine 'peethas'.

extra_sections.label: Which nine?
extra_sections.h2: Which are the 9 Devis of the Nau Devi Yatra?
extra_sections.html:
1 · Shakumbhari Devi
शाकुम्भरी देवी

Behat, Saharanpur (UP), in the Shivalik foothills. Pilgrims first visit Bhura Dev, the guardian Bhairav, about 1 km before the main shrine.

2 · Mata Mansa Devi
मनसा देवी

Panchkula, Haryana, run by the Mata Mansa Devi Shrine Board. This is the Panchkula temple — not Mansa Devi of Haridwar.

3 · Kali Mata, Kalka
काली माता, कालका

In Kalka town at the foot of the Shimla hills, about 25 km from Mansa Devi and managed by the same Shrine Board.

4 · Naina Devi
नैना देवी

A Shivalik hilltop in Bilaspur, Himachal — Suzu's home district. A cable car climbs from the base. Not the Naina Devi of Nainital. Full Naina Devi guide.

5 · Chintpurni
चिंतपूर्णी

Chhaproh in Una district, seat of Chhinnamastika. Join the queue with a darshan slip (parchi) from the guard.

6 · Jwala Ji
ज्वाला जी

Jawalamukhi, Kangra: no idol, only flames from the rock. Devotees see the Devi in them; geologists describe natural gas seeping from the ground.

7 · Brajeshwari (Kangra Devi)
ब्रजेश्वरी

Kangra town, old Nagarkot. Rebuilt after the 1905 earthquake; the pindi is covered in butter every Makar Sankranti.

8 · Chamunda Nandikeshwar Dham
चामुंडा

On the Baner river near Dharamshala, below the Dhauladhar range.

9 · Mata Vaishno Devi
वैष्णो देवी

The cave shrine on Trikuta hill above Katra, Jammu & Kashmir — the eldest of the sisters and the last, steepest stop of the yatra.

The package variant. Many tour operators drop Kalka and Shakumbhari and add Baglamukhi (Bankhandi, between Jwala Ji and Kangra) and a Sheetla Devi temple. Neither list is “official” — choose by your route and time. Nau Devi is not Navadurga: Navadurga are the nine forms of Durga worshipped on the nine nights; the Nau Devi Yatra is a journey to nine temples.

darshan.h2: Darshan timings at the nine Devi temples
rows: Summer 4 am – 10 pm, winter 5 am – 9 pm. Aarti: summer 4:30 am & 7 pm, winter 5:30 am & 6 pm (Shrine Board).
Summer 4 am – 10 pm, winter 5 am – 9 pm (Mansa Devi Shrine Board).
4 am – 10 pm; 2 am – midnight during Navratri (temple trust).
Hours and aarti times are not published — confirm locally. Darshan slip from the guard; paid Sugam Darshan can be booked on the trust's site.
Roughly 5–6 am to 10 pm with a short midday break (official sources differ — confirm locally).
Open round the clock, except during the morning and evening aarti.
darshan.note: From the shrine boards, temple trusts, district administrations and Incredible India, checked 8–9 Oct 2026. Hours stretch during Navratri and the melas — always confirm on the day.

dates.note: Navratri is the most auspicious time for the nine Devis — and the most crowded. Start each day early, book stays ahead, and keep a spare day. The Vaishno Devi Shrine Board asks pilgrims not to trek during weather alerts.

route.h2: Nau Devi Yatra route, with road distances
route.lead: The classic order runs from the Shivalik foothills of UP and Haryana up into Himachal's Kangra valley, and ends at Trikuta hill in Jammu. Distances are by road.
route.video_caption: Nine Devis across four states and union territories. The order below saves backtracking; the reverse works too — start at Vaishno Devi from Jammu (Katra is about 50 km away) and end at Shakumbhari.
stops: North to Behat in Saharanpur district; darshan at Bhura Dev first.
Across the Yamuna to Panchkula, next to Chandigarh.
A short drive — both are easy on the same day.
Into Himachal via Anandpur Sahib; cable car to the hilltop.
Down to Una and up to Chhaproh.
Baglamukhi at Bankhandi is on the way if you want a tenth darshan.
Via Pathankot to Katra; the trek is about 12 km each way. Katra back to Delhi is about 649 km.
route.note: Road distances from OpenStreetMap routing, 8 Oct 2026. Real hill driving takes 30–60% longer than map estimates — allow extra time.

reach.h2: How to start and end the Nau Devi Yatra
cards: Drive north to Shakumbhari (about 210 km) and follow the route above; return from Katra by road, train or air from Jammu.
Mansa Devi and Kalka are on the city's doorstep, and Naina Devi is about 100 km away — the usual start for the 7-day package route.
Chandigarh airport for the start, Gaggal (Kangra) airport near Brajeshwari and Chamunda, and Jammu airport for Vaishno Devi.
Kalka, Anandpur Sahib (for Naina Devi), Pathankot for Kangra, and Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra station at the end.
Suzu Travels is based in Bilaspur district, about 64 km from Naina Devi — we plan the Himachal leg of this yatra every Navratri.

itinerary.h2: A 9-day Nau Devi Yatra itinerary from Delhi
days: About 210 km. Darshan at Bhura Dev and Shakumbhari; overnight near Saharanpur.
About 156 km to Panchkula, darshan at Mansa Devi, then 25 km to Kalka. Overnight in Panchkula or Chandigarh.
About 110 km into Himachal, cable car up, evening darshan. Overnight at Naina Devi or Anandpur Sahib.
About 112 km. Darshan with a parchi; overnight at Chintpurni or nearby.
31 km to the flames of Jwala Ji, then 36 km to Kangra. Overnight in Kangra or Dharamshala.
Morning darshan at Kangra Devi, then 22 km to Chamunda. Evening in Dharamshala.
About 241 km via Pathankot. Collect the RFID Yatra Access Card and rest.
Trek (or helicopter / battery car where available) to the Bhawan, darshan, then Bhairon temple; back to Katra.
Drive to Jammu for a flight or train, or back to Delhi (about 649 km).

items: The free RFID Yatra Access Card is compulsory — one per pilgrim, from the Katra counters or the only official site, online.maavaishnodevi.org. Start the climb within the time limit printed on your card (recent reports differ, so check the Shrine Board). Beware of fake booking sites.
The helicopter flies Katra–Sanjichhat, not to the Bhawan; book only through the Shrine Board portal. Battery cars and the Bhawan–Bhairon ropeway also run.
Take the darshan slip from the temple guard and use only the official queue — no back-door darshan. Please don't feed the monkeys.
Choose 9 days over 7, travel outside Navratri and Shravan, use the Naina Devi cable car and the Vaishno Devi helicopter or battery-car quotas. Vaishno Devi helpline: 1800-180-7212 (toll-free).
Photo ID (needed for the RFID card), a light bag, grippy shoes, a rain poncho, a warm layer, cash/UPI, and printed hotel bookings in Navratri.
Modest clothes, shoes off at the gate. At Vaishno Devi, shoes and belts are not allowed in the holy cave — use the free cloak room at the Bhawan.

faq_h2: Nau Devi Yatra: questions pilgrims ask
faqs: Which are the 9 Devis of the Nau Devi Yatra?

Traditionally Vaishno Devi, Mansa Devi (Panchkula), Kali Mata of Kalka, Shakumbhari Devi, Naina Devi, Chintpurni, Jwala Ji, Kangra Devi (Brajeshwari) and Chamunda. Many packages swap Kalka and Shakumbhari for Baglamukhi and a Sheetla Devi temple.
How many days does the Nau Devi Yatra take?
About 9 days from Delhi for all nine temples. The common package route of seven Devis, starting from Chandigarh, takes about 7 days.
What is the best route order for the 9 Devi Yatra?
Shakumbhari → Mansa Devi → Kalka → Naina Devi → Chintpurni → Jwala Ji → Kangra → Chamunda → Vaishno Devi. The reverse also works, starting at Vaishno Devi from Jammu.
Is the Nau Devi Yatra the same as Navadurga?
No. Navadurga are the nine forms of Durga worshipped on the nine nights of Navratri. The Nau Devi Yatra is a journey to nine different Devi temples.
Are all nine temples Shakti Peeths?

No. Naina Devi, Jwala Ji and Kangra Devi appear in the classical lists, and Chintpurni's place is disputed. Vaishno Devi, Mansa Devi, Chamunda, Kalka and Shakumbhari are revered by their own traditions.
Do I need registration for the Nau Devi Yatra?
Only for Vaishno Devi: the free RFID Yatra Access Card, from the Katra counters or online.maavaishnodevi.org. Start the climb within the time limit printed on your card.
What is the best time for the Nau Devi Yatra?
March–June and September–November. Navratri (Sharad Navratri 2026 begins on 11 October) is the most auspicious time but also the most crowded; avoid peak monsoon.
Can elderly parents do the Nau Devi Yatra?
Yes, with planning: take 9 days rather than 7, use the Naina Devi cable car and the Vaishno Devi helicopter or battery-car options, and travel outside Navratri and Shravan.
